purpose: Methods literature for evidence retrieval, structured investigation, reconstruction and prospective institutional forecasting; not a corpus of guilt labels or a claim that all books were read in full.

sources.title: Psychology of Intelligence Analysis
sources.publisher: CIA Center for the Study of Intelligence
sources.access: Original PDF downloaded and converted with pdftotext; selected chapters and passages inspected.
locators: Chapter 5, Do You Really Need More Information?, pp. 51–64
Chapter 8, Analysis of Competing Hypotheses, pp. 95–110; step outline p. 97
Chapter 13, Hindsight Biases in Evaluation of Intelligence Reporting, pp. 161–172
sources.inspectedFinding: Consider multiple hypotheses, evidence diagnosticity and sensitivity to key assumptions; preserve the original judgment because outcome knowledge changes retrospective evaluation.
implementation: Rival hypotheses and disconfirming observations
Immutable forecast-as-of ledger
Qualitative priority for records that discriminate between live explanations
limitations: A classic analytical-method book, not evidence that ACH improves this model's accuracy
Human cognitive mechanisms cannot simply be assumed to transfer to language models
Historical examples are not contemporary findings about named Indian actors

sources.title: Confirmation Bias: A Ubiquitous Phenomenon in Many Guises
sources.access: Exa clean-text extraction of the university-hosted paper; abstract and opening evidence-review sections inspected, not the complete paper.
locators: Opening discussion of biased evidence seeking/interpretation
Discussion of hypothesis testing and alternative hypotheses in the inspected opening extraction
sources.inspectedFinding: Confirmation bias includes seeking and interpreting information in ways that favor existing beliefs or a hypothesis in hand.
implementation: Separate hypothesis author and challenger
Require counterevidence queries and preserve their results
Do not count confirmatory search volume as independent support
limitations: Review of human psychological research rather than a benchmark of AI research agents
A prompted challenger is not established to eliminate bias

sources.title: The analysis of competing hypotheses in intelligence analysis
sources.access: Exa extracted article text; abstract, methods, accuracy results and discussion inspected. Publication date checked against publisher entry.
locators: Accuracy analyses comparing ACH and untrained groups
Discussion of application, consistency and error
sources.inspectedFinding: Fifty intelligence analysts were randomly allocated; evidence for reducing confirmation bias was mixed, and ACH use could increase inconsistency and error. The ACH group was not significantly more accurate in selecting the correct hypothesis in this task.
implementation: Keep alternative-hypothesis worksheets auditable
Do not derive probabilities by adding ordinal consistency marks
Evaluate actual downstream error rather than count completed checklist steps
limitations: One controlled task and analyst population do not establish that every structured technique fails
Many participants deviated from prescribed steps
This challenges efficacy claims, not the utility of documenting alternatives

sources.title: Psychological Strategies for Winning a Geopolitical Forecasting Tournament
sources.access: Official society article abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected via Exa; complete paywalled article not acquired.
locators: Publisher first-online date and May 2014 issue metadata
sources.inspectedFinding: A two-year geopolitical forecasting tournament found support for probability training, teaming and performance tracking, with improvements in calibration and resolution.
implementation: Record forecasts and resolved outcomes
Compare a reference class before case-specific adjustment
Track independent rationales and update histories
limitations: The inspected abstract does not support reconstructing all experimental details
Human-team tournament effects do not validate same-model AI swarms
No effect size from this study is claimed for the local model

sources.title: Superforecasting: The Art and Science of Prediction
sources.access: Publisher book description and edition dates inspected; no full book downloaded or claimed as fully read.
sources.inspectedFinding: The authorized description emphasizes varied evidence, probabilistic thinking, teamwork, keeping score and willingness to revise beliefs.
implementation: Accessible reading recommendation
Explicit forecast revisions and reasons
Methods claims anchored in original tournament research rather than endorsements
limitations: Publisher description is a summary and promotional material, not the full empirical study
Book publicity is not evidence that a trained embedding model forecasts future events

sources.title: Causal Inference: What If
sources.publisher: Author-hosted revised book; suggested citation remains Hernán and Robins (2020), Chapman & Hall/CRC
sources.access: Author page and linked PDF downloaded; title page confirms August 19, 2026. Contents and selected causal-inference/time-zero passages inspected.
locators: Section 3.6 The target trial, p. 41 onward
sources.inspectedFinding: Association and causal effects are different estimands; target-trial emulation must align eligibility, treatment strategy assignment and start of follow-up. Misaligned time zero can introduce selection bias.
implementation: Separate retrospective reconstruction from causal claims
Explicit population, target and prediction time
Preserve feature availability before follow-up and outcome
limitations: The book's causal identification assumptions are not met merely by creating a graph
The selected case corpus is not a target-trial dataset
Free access is not permission to republish or relicense the full copyrighted book
The older April 2024 indexed PDF was not used as the latest edition

sources.title: Story-Based Inquiry: A Manual for Investigative Journalists
sources.access: Author-hosted PDF downloaded and converted; introduction, hypothesis chapter and quality-control discussion inspected. UNESCO metadata identifies 2011 edition and CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO.
locators: Chapter 2, Using hypotheses: The core of investigative method
sources.inspectedFinding: A story begins as a hypothesis; break it into specific claims that can be verified or disproved, and organize the source material for later quality control.
implementation: Atomic claims linked to locators
Source and contradiction ledger
Publishable claims distinguished from reporting questions
limitations: A reporting method is not a calibrated prediction model
Narrative coherence adds no independent evidence
No interviews or external information requests were sent by this review

sources.title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
sources.publisher: Journal of the American Statistical Association, 102(477)
sources.access: Exa extraction of author-hosted paper; abstract, introduction and proper-scoring definitions inspected.
locators: Definition of proper and strictly proper scoring rules
sources.inspectedFinding: Proper scoring rules reward honest predictive distributions in expectation; strictly proper rules have a unique optimum at the true distribution. Forecast quality is evaluated against realized outcomes, with calibration distinguished from concentration/sharpness.
implementation: Brier and log-loss evaluation for resolved binary targets
Calibration and baseline comparisons
No probability claims from similarity scores or unresolved scenarios
limitations: A proper metric does not correct selective sampling, leakage or wrong outcome labels
A small selected case set cannot establish national calibration

sources.title: ForecastBench: A Dynamic Benchmark of AI Forecasting Capabilities
sources.publisher: ICLR 2025; Forecasting Research Institute revised-paper page
sources.access: Official abstract/revision dates and current official documentation inspected. Page records initial publication September 30, 2024 and revision February 28, 2025.
locators: Official docs: Latest version of paper, Architecture and Leaderboards
sources.inspectedFinding: Forecasting questions unresolved at submission enable genuinely prospective evaluation. The benchmark is continuously refreshed and separates forecasting accuracy from static question-answering knowledge.
implementation: Preregister unresolved institutional outcomes
Immutable submission and resolution timestamps
Treat historical reconstruction as a different evaluation task
limitations: Neither this project nor its MiniLM retriever was evaluated on ForecastBench
The original study's comparative model results are historical, not a claim about October 2026 rankings
A 2026 university upload directory was not treated as a newly published 2026 paper

sources.title: ForecastBench: Updated Ranking Methodology
sources.dateBasis: Last-updated date on official ForecastBench documentation for the linked addendum
sources.access: Original PDF downloaded and converted; abstract, sections 2, 4.3 and 6 inspected.
sources.inspectedFinding: Unadjusted scores can confound model ability with question difficulty when forecasters answer different sets; the proposed adjustment uses a model of question difficulty and reports limitations involving domain skill and estimation assumptions.
implementation: Prefer paired identical-question comparisons in the local pilot
Report denominator and coverage
Do not rank changing case sets as if they were directly comparable
limitations: The adjustment is not a solution to a tiny selected corpus
Assumptions of stable cross-domain forecaster ability can fail
The documented 50-day leaderboard waiting period is specific to that benchmark and is not imported as a local calibration guarantee

sources.title: Approaching Human-Level Forecasting with Language Models
sources.access: Original arXiv HTML extracted; abstract, retrieval/reasoning/aggregation sections and evaluation discussion inspected.
locators: Retrieval: query generation, retrieval, relevance filtering, summarization
Selective forecasting and crowd combination discussion
sources.inspectedFinding: The paper separates retrieval, reasoning and aggregation. On its reported full test setting, the system's average Brier score was 0.179 versus the human crowd's 0.149; selective or combined settings are separate analyses.
implementation: Do not equate a retriever with the full forecasting system
Declare selective forecasting and abstention coverage
Preserve temporal information barriers and validation-only tuning
limitations: Results used different models and forecasting-platform data, not MiniLM or Indian procurement
A claim of approaching crowd performance is not a claim of general superiority
Pretraining overlap of our model remains unknown

sources.title: Red Flags in Public Procurement: A Guide to Using Data to Detect and Mitigate Risks
sources.access: Official PDF clean-text extraction and official publication page inspected; definition, implementation/validation guidance and relevant indicator families read.
locators: Indicator annex: R018, R032, R033, R053, R064–R073
sources.inspectedFinding: The guide maps 73 procurement indicators to OCDS fields and explicitly states a flag signals risk rather than evidence of illicit behavior. Interpretation must consider legal framework, context and false positives.
implementation: Use measurable tender/bid/award/contract variables with denominators
Keep missingness distinct from zero
Collect original records before computing ownership, amendment or payment indicators
limitations: The 73 indicators were not all implemented or computed in this methods review
Selected narrative summaries are not a complete OCDS dataset
No universal threshold or scalar corruption probability follows from a flag

sources.title: OECD Guidelines for Fighting Bid Rigging in Public Procurement (2025 Update): Bid-Rigging Detection List
sources.access: Official full chapter extracted; warning-sign sections and caution about indicators inspected.
locators: Section 3.6: A caution about indicators of bid rigging
Section 3.7: keeping detailed records and reviewing history
sources.inspectedFinding: Repeated bidding patterns, shared metadata and pricing anomalies are investigation cues, but are not proof. Capacity constraints and different cost estimates are explicit ordinary explanations.
implementation: Preserve exact bid files, dates and metadata provenance
Compare repeated patterns within a defined market
Require ordinary explanations and follow-up records before alleging coordination
limitations: Guidance for procurement/competition authorities does not authorize us to accuse firms
Same IP, common templates or frequent wins do not establish collusion
No competition authority was contacted by this review

accessNotes: Research used official/author/university materials and authorized summaries; full copyrighted books are not committed or relicensed.
Exa search results were followed by page/PDF extraction for source inspection; metadata dates are distinguished from current retrieval dates.
The separate ForecastBench /changelog/ URL did not yield a usable fetched result; no finding relies on it. Official documentation and its linked methodology PDF were inspected instead.

Lindley's 1956 information paper was located but not retained as an inspected primary source because the original provider was blocked; acquisition priority remains qualitative rather than claiming formal expected information gain.
This literature register documents methods, not model-training inputs, verified network edges or measured performance improvements.
